brief: JPM's accelerating deposit costs and a 10% FICC trading miss were offset by cutting buybacks to ~$1bn to redeploy capital into risk-weighted assets, with 2027 NII guidance of $107bn (+10% YoY) seen as the bull thesis anchor. WFC's EPS beat was discounted as tax-driven while a PPNR miss and a CET1 slip to 10.0% point toward further buyback cuts. The capital gap versus JPM's 13.9% CET1 is expected to force lower-capital banks to pause buybacks while money-center banks keep flexibility to fund AI buildouts. GS forecasts 2027 primary equity issuance of $600bn (0.8% of market cap) and buybacks rising to $1.7tn, alongside $1.2tn of hyperscaler capex (35% debt-funded, over $400bn of issuance). Rising rates are flagged as a risk to buyback growth. For September, GS expects core CPI +0.24% m/m but a cooler +2.46% YoY, with headline CPI accelerating to +3.70% YoY on energy and food. Implied correlation sits near 20-year lows into earnings despite low GS PB net exposure, implying stock selection will matter if investors re-risk. Widening French, Italian and UK sovereign spreads lead GS to expect elevated European sovereign volatility, tracked via the GSXESOVR basket rather than the more diluted SX7P.
